title: From Nested Soliton Crystals to Skyrmion Crystals in Chiral Magnets
abstract: We perform an exhaustive study of the parameter space of the chiral magnetic model with a Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, an in-plane anisotropy term and an out-of-plane Zeeman magnetic field. We map out the phase diagram for the model and find a chiral soliton lattice hosted on a chiral soliton lattice as the ground state in a particular corner of the phase diagram. There is a smooth crossover, as opposed to a phase transition, to the skyrmion crystal lattice phase. Finally, we also discover excited composite soliton states such as an anti-skyrmion coexisting with a bimeron or an anti-bimeron.
summary: This paper exhaustively maps the phase diagram of a chiral magnetic model incorporating Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and external fields. The key finding is that the transition between nested soliton crystal and skyrmion crystal phases is a smooth crossover. The work provides detailed theoretical insights into the stability and interaction of various topological magnetic textures.
main_problem: The study investigates the phase diagram of a chiral magnetic model to understand the transition between different soliton crystal phases.
main_result: The research finds that the transition from a chiral soliton lattice hosted on a chiral soliton lattice (CSL on a CSL) to the skyrmion crystal lattice (SkX) occurs via a smooth crossover, not a sharp phase transition.
method: The authors performed an exhaustive study by mapping out the phase diagram of the model across its parameter space.
model_or_system: The system is a chiral magnet described by an energy functional involving a Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, in-plane anisotropy, and an out-of-plane Zeeman field. The dynamics are governed by an equation of motion derived from this energy functional.
key_observables: Topological charge (Skyrmion number), ground state energy, and the existence/stability of various soliton structures (skyrmions, bimerons, domain walls).
important_parameters: The dimensionless parameters K (in-plane anisotropy) and B (out-of-plane Zeeman field) define the phase diagram.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the parameter space and treating the transition between phases as a smooth crossover rather than a first-order phase transition.
figures_summary: The notes mention a phase diagram (Fig. 1(b)) illustrating the crossover between different magnetic phases.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the energy functional, derives the equations of motion for various topological structures (DWs, skyrmions), maps the resulting phase diagram, and identifies the nature of the transitions between the observed ground states.
why_interesting: The study of continuous crossovers between ordered magnetic phases, especially those involving topological defects like skyrmions, provides rich theoretical models relevant to understanding phase transitions in quantum materials.

The figures also show the anti-skyrmion energies, but relative to the anti-DW’s energy as they live on the anti-DW. In panel (a), the bimeron and anti-skyrmion’s energies are degenerate. Negative bimeron energies make it the ground state, whereas the positive energy states are excited states of the DW. The colors of the curves match the soliton type in Fig. 1.

FIG. 3. CSL on CSL phase (strong condition): K = 0.42, B = 0.8. The four panels display the magnetization vector n, the DMI energy density E1, the total energy density E and finally the topological charge density Q. The coloring scheme of the magnetization vector: n = e3 is white, n = −e3 is black, n = e1 is red, n = e2 is light green, n = −e1 is cyan and n = −e2 is violet. The energy of the solution in this figure is minimized with respect to the dimensions in both the x- and the y-direction subject to periodic boundary conditions. A single bimeron is marked with a dashed line in all panels.
